title: Pick the tweezers that fit and peel a phone's screen film off by its folded end
instruction: Two pairs of tweezers stand in their holders. A smartphone lies screen-up in a loose carrier, and the end of its blue protective film is folded down over the phone's bottom edge into a narrow channel. Use the pair whose tips fit the relief cut at the centre of that fold to grasp the folded film and peel the film off the screen, while holding the loose carrier still. Lay the film on the table outside the carrier, put both pairs of tweezers back upright in their own holders, and move both hands away.
context: Phone assembly and rework benches keep several tweezers: paddle tips for handling film on open surfaces, fine tips for tight spaces. Here the film has no pull tab: its own end is folded over the phone's bottom edge and hangs in the carrier's 6 mm relief channel, narrower than the robot's closed fingertips (7.9 mm). A 5.6 mm relief cut at the centre of the fold lets the fine tips (2.4 mm) reach behind the film, while the paddle tips (7 mm) land on the fold. The robot has to pick the fine-tip pair, open and close the passive spring tweezers through its own grip, pinch the film itself and peel while the other hand keeps the unclamped carrier from sliding or lifting, then set the film aside and put the tools back. Gripper-only attempts and the paddle-tip pair release no film.
setup: Dual-YAM station on a 1.10 x 1.30 x 0.06 m oak table, centre (0.36,0,0.7175) m, top z=0.7475 m. Arm bases (0,+/-0.305,0.75) m, left at +y, facing +x. A loose POM phone carrier, 250 g with the phone clamped in it, occupies x=0.225..0.335, y=-0.21..0.14, z=0.7475..0.7645 m; its base is 3 mm thick. A 71.5 x 147 x 7.8 mm smartphone (graphite aluminium frame, 9 mm corner radius, black glass screen) lies screen-up in its pocket at x=0.244..0.316, y=-0.202..-0.055, screen top z=0.7625. Side rails and the front support flange (from y=-0.049) rise to z=0.7645. A 6 mm relief channel, y=-0.055..-0.049, runs across the phone's bottom end down to the base. Blue PE protective film, 66 x 140 mm, covers the screen at x=0.247..0.313, y=-0.195..-0.055. Its first 15 mm from the bottom edge (y=-0.070..-0.055) is a non-adhesive starter zone; the other 125 mm is stuck to the glass. The film's end is folded down over the phone's bottom edge: a 66 x 10 x 1 mm flap hangs in the channel, centred (0.28,-0.052,0.7580) m, 2.5 mm from the phone and from the carrier. A 5.6 mm relief cut at the centre of the fold (x=0.2772..0.2828) leaves the gap behind the flap open there. A 15 g stainless-steel tweezer tool, 120 mm long, has 2.4 x 0.8 mm tips and rests open 8 mm, pointing down in an ABS stand centred (0.36,-0.24). Stand floor is 30 x 34 x 3 mm; four 3 mm thick walls rise 20 mm above z=0.7505. A second, otherwise identical tool with 7 x 0.8 mm paddle tips stands open in an identical stand centred (0.36,-0.17). Both stands are fixed. Exact component bounds and the fixed starting layout are in fixture_geometry.py and tool_geometry.py.
scoring: Any carrier excursion beyond 30 mm horizontally, 5 mm vertically or 10 degrees yaw/tilt, or film seam separation beyond 3 mm, makes the trial score 0. Consecutive peeled adhesive length, from the starter zone: <30 mm: 0; >=30 mm: 0.25; >=60 mm: 0.5; >=90 mm: 0.75. Full credit requires all 125 mm of adhesive detached; every film piece at least 2 mm outside the carrier, within 30 mm above the tabletop, with table support; each tweezer tool's tip centre within 4.5 mm horizontally (inside its own stand's cavity) and 5 mm vertically of that stand's target, tilt <=5 degrees and tip opening 6-10 mm. Tools must move below 10 mm/s and 0.5 rad/s, no film piece may move over 2 mm or turn over 5 degrees, and both TCPs must be at least 80 mm from every task object, for 1 second.
reset_notes: Use a fresh protective film with the same folded end and relief cut for each physical trial. Place the carrier flat with the phone clamped in its pocket, and both open tools upright in their stands. Simulator reset restores all poses and adhesive joints; use object_jitter=0 and seed 0.
fidelity: PhysX at 240 Hz. Film: 28 rigid 5 mm strips (first three non-adhesive) and a rigid folded end, 1 mm thick; the end is simulated at 3 g for stable tweezer contact. Peel-front springs (0.025 N m/rad) release above 60 degrees at 20 Hz, not fitted to measured adhesion. Tweezer halves slide on a 150 N/m spring; contact alone grasps a tool. The phone is clamped in the carrier (one rigid body); carrier friction 0.4. No stretch, wrinkles, tearing or ESD. Carrier and fold cut are benchmark-designed.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,400 steps, step limit); scripted demo: 1.0 (1,298 steps).
